drills.q: Sketch the QuantLib object graph that prices a European call — list every object in order.
drills.a: Quote (spot) -> YieldTermStructure (flat or bootstrapped) -> BlackVolTermStructure (flat or BlackVarianceSurface) -> BlackScholesMertonProcess(the three) -> EuropeanOption(PlainVanillaPayoff, EuropeanExercise) -> setPricingEngine(AnalyticEuropeanEngine) -> NPV(), delta(), gamma(), vega(), theta().

drills.q: Your QuantLib price differs from the desk's by 0.3%. Where do you look FIRST?
drills.a: Day counts (Actual365Fixed vs Thirty360 vs ActualActual), calendars (holiday sets), and curve conventions (compounding, settlement days) — the conventions are where the money hides; the formula is the one thing certainly right. That's why 'the diff is where the day counts hide' is the interview-safe line.

drills.q: Write the cvxpy long-only fully-invested min-variance problem from memory.
drills.a: w = cp.Variable(n); risk = cp.quad_form(w, Sigma); prob = cp.Problem(cp.Minimize(risk), [cp.sum(w) == 1, w >= 0]); prob.solve(). DCP verifies convexity BEFORE solving — non-PSD Sigma raises, unlike SLSQP which returns garbage silently.

drills.q: A colleague's portfolio weights jump wildly between quarterly rebalances. Diagnose and fix.
drills.a: Estimation error in mu/S amplified by the optimizer — max-Sharpe is the worst amplifier. Fix the INPUT: Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage on S, Black-Litterman on mu (market prior + views), or HRP which needs no inversion. Then run the bootstrap-stability check: 500 resamples of mu, watch weights scatter.

drills.q: Extract implied vol from a 6M option trading at 4.50 when BS-at-30%-vol gives 4.20. Mechanics?
drills.a: brentq on f(v) = BS_price(v) - 4.50, bracketed [0.01, 3] — monotone in v, so bracketing is safe. Deep ITM/OTM: price-vol curve flattens -> inversion unstable, that's the smile near expiry. Or QuantLib's built-in implied-vol helpers.

drills.q: Fit GARCH(1,1) on daily returns and interpret alpha=0.09, beta=0.89.
drills.a: arch_model(r, vol='GARCH', p=1, q=1, dist='t').fit(). alpha+beta = 0.98 = persistence near IGARCH — shocks decay very slowly (vol clustering). Output: conditional_volatility path (one sigma/day), forecastable h steps ahead. Rolling std would be a window statistic, not this.

drills.q: Your barrier-option Monte Carlo takes 40s in pure Python. Fix it in order.
drills.a: 1) Vectorize the path generation (array shape (n_paths, n_steps)) — but barrier logic is path-dependent, so... 2) @njit(parallel=True, cache=True, fastmath=True) the path loop -> ~100-500x, ~0.2s. 3) GPU/JAX batch only if homogeneous paths at serious scale. Never Numba before attempting vectorization.

drills.q: Colleague reran your simulation notebook, got different numbers. What did you do wrong?
drills.a: Global legacy RNG (np.random.seed) instead of an explicit Generator(PCG64(seed)) — global state breaks under parallelism and cell-reordering; possibly also unpinned library versions. Model validation rejects code for exactly this: set the evaluation date, pin the generator, lock the versions.

drills.q: Greeks for a portfolio of 50 options — finite differences need 200 MC runs. Better?
drills.a: Autodiff: JAX grad through the pricing graph — one forward+backward pass gives all Greeks (pathwise differentiation), replacing the 4x-paths finite-difference stencil. This is the modern convergence of the library conversation and the derivatives math.

drills.q: Your backtest signals don't match the trading platform's chart RSI. Debug order.
drills.a: Convention mismatch first: TA-Lib's RSI is WILDER smoothing (alpha=1/n recursive), not SMA-of-changes; then warmup periods, adjusted-vs-raw closes, and field/schema drift if data sources differ. Indicator conventions before strategy logic, every time.

drills.q: You have no views. What does Black-Litterman reduce to, and why is that the right answer?
drills.a: The market prior — reverse-optimized equilibrium returns from cap weights. BL is a better ESTIMATOR not a better solver; with no views there's nothing to blend, and the prior IS the estimate. Knowing the formula collapses is the understanding.

drills.q: Name the tiers: non-negotiable / extremely valuable / powerful-but-situational.
drills.a: Non-negotiable: NumPy, SciPy, Statsmodels, QuantLib, cvxpy. Extremely valuable: scikit-learn, Numba, PyTorch/JAX, pyarrow/polars. Powerful-but-situational: arch, PyPortfolioOpt, TA-Lib, yfinance. Bottom line: your desk determines what matters most; the mistake isn't the wrong library — it's learning libraries instead of the mathematics underneath.
